rules.answer_text: Right, so — I was down the alley end around then. Saw someone in a blue coat come in from the square about a quarter to... no, closer to ten-to. Went towards the cafe's back door. Didn't see the face but — that's Nadia Cole's coat, everyone knows it. And later there was this thud from inside. Dull, like a sack of flour going over. I didn't think anything of it. You don't, do you.

claims.summary: Clara Wells says she saw someone in a blue coat — she assumes Nadia Cole — enter the alley at about 10:33 and head for the cafe's rear door.
Clara Wells says she heard a dull thud from the cafe's back rooms while she was in the alley, around 10:42.

rules.answer_text: From about twenty to eight I was at the clinic — Ben Carter was taking my blood pressure, of all things. I'd been wound up about the meeting. I left just before eight, waited here at a table, and at ten past I went looking for him myself. I found him.

rules.answer_text: So it's true. Marcus Bell. He promised me that expansion two years ago — I built my plans on it. If you're asking whether I was angry: yes. Angry enough to demand a meeting. Not angry enough for... whatever you're implying. I was with Ben Carter when it happened, ask him.

claims.summary: Isabella Reed admits the partnership betrayal gave her a grievance, but points to her clinic alibi.

rules.answer_text: From a quarter past seven I was in my yard. Timber delivery came — big one. Driver, Col Hartley, was with me signing sheets and unloading until gone eight. Check with them if you don't believe me. I've nothing to hide about where I was.

rules.answer_text: Eight thousand. There, I've said the number. They'd have ruined me by lunchtime and called it principle. But I was in my yard with Col when it happened, and thank God for that delivery, because I know how this looks.

rules.answer_text: ...Alright. Please don't take this the wrong way. I was in the alley, for a few minutes, around a quarter to eight. With Clara Wells. We've been seeing each other — Isabella Reed doesn't approve of that kind of thing at the shop, so we keep it quiet. We stood by the back door and talked, that's all. We heard a sort of thud from the cafe side and then a door, and we got nervous someone would see us, so we left. Clara Wells went to her van. I went inside. That's everything, I promise.

rules.answer_text: Forty years I knew them. And I'll tell you something for nothing: last week, in the cafe, I heard them say to somebody — quiet, but furious, the way they got — 'You have until tomorrow.' Never saw who. Kitchen doorway, my back was to it. But Elias Grant didn't threaten people for sport. Somebody in this village was living on borrowed time, and I'd say the loan came due.

claims.summary: Priya Shah heard Elias Grant tell someone 'You have until tomorrow' in the cafe last week, but didn't see who.

suggested_followups: Could it have been a member of staff they was talking to?

rules.answer_text: Nadia Cole went out the front just before the quarter hour and turned towards the square. Now here's the thing — she says village square, I hear. I face that village square, young detective. My eyes aren't what they were, and I did have my crossword. But I don't recall seeing her at it. Owen Price, though — you should have heard him this morning. That's your man, I'd stake my pension.

claims.summary: Priya Shah, who faces the fountain from her bench, does not recall seeing Nadia Cole at the fountain between 10:31 and 10:46 — though she admits her attention was on her crossword.
Priya Shah insists Owen Price must be the killer because of the morning argument.
